JUDGMENT 1.

By this judgment, the present DAR (Detailed Accident Report) filed by the Investigting Agency,
which has been treated as claim petition under section 166(4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, on behalf of the petitioner, shall be decided.

The important facts of the case, as per DAR, are that the Shadab suffered injuries on account of a motor vehicular accident happened on 07.10.2018 at about 23:40 hours, on road in front of Jain Mandir Jhuggi, near Meera Baba Peer, Dilshad Colony, Delhi.

On the aforesaid date and time, the petitioner Shadab along with his friend Ajeem was going on the motorcycle bearing no.
CG04-DJ-8292.
The motorcycle was being driven by Shadab, and Ajeem was sitting as pillion.

When they reached the aforesaid place, a garbage lifter truck of EDMC bearing registration no.

1 DL1GC-1065 (hereinafter, "offending vehicle") being driven by the respondent no.1 Pawan at a very high speed and in rash and negligent manner, came and hit the motorcycle from behind.

As a result,
the motorcyclists along with the motorcycle fell down on the road.
Motorcycle got damaged and the petitioner suffered in his hand.
Ajeem got the truck driver/ respondent no.1 apprehended with the help of public persons.
PCR police came to the spot, as someone from public had called at 100 number.
The injured/ petitioner was removed to GTB Hospital, where his MLC was prepared.

3. In respect of this accident, the criminal case vide FIR No. 565/2018, under sections 279/337, IPC,
was registered at PS Seemapuri, Delhi on 08.10.2018 on the statement of the petitioner.
During investigation, it was found out that at the time of the accident, the offending vehicle, which was being driven by respondent no.1, was owned by respondent no.2 and it was not insured.

5. Respondent no.1 in his written statement stated that the alleged accident was a result of the negligence of the injured himself and not of the answering respondent.

It is stated that the injured was hit by another vehicle due to which the answering respondent stopped his vehicle at the spot and the injured got the respondent falsely implicated in this case.
6.

In the written statement filed on behalf of the respondent no.2/ EDMC, it is stated that the petitioner is not entitled to any claim from the answering respondent, as no accident had taken place due to the negligence of the respondent no.1.
7.

DL-1GC-1065, being driven by respondent no.1/ driver?

The Investigating Officer/ ASI Om Prakash was examined under section 168 of Bhartiya Sakshya Adhiniyam by this Tribunal.
11. I heard the final arguments advanced by learned counsels for the parties and also pursued the evidence and other materials placed on record.

My findings on the issues are as under:-

3 ISSUE NO.1

Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 07.10.2018 at about 23:40 hours in front of Jain Mandir, Jhuggi Meera Baba Peer, on road towards Old Seemapuri Road, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing no.
DL-1GC-1065, being driven by respondent no.1/ driver? OPP 12.
On this issue, it is seen that the PW1 Pawan Kumar, the injured/ petitioner, himself, entered into the witness box being an eye-witness of the accident and deposed that on the lines of the FIR.
PW1 stated that on 07.10.2018 at about 11:10 p.m., he along with his friend Ajeem was going on his motorcycle bearing no. CG04-DJ-8292, being driven by him and Ajeem was sitting on pillion seat.

PW1 stated that when they reached in front of Jain Mandir Jhuggi, near Meera Baba Peer, Dilshad Colony, Delhi, a truck of EDMC bearing registration no. DL1GC-1065 being driven by the r e s p o n d e n t  
n o .
1 ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 674/2018; Shadab v. Pawan Kumar & Anr. 5 of 20 Pages Pawan at a very high speed and in rash and negligent manner, came and hit the motorcycle from behind.
As a result, the petitioner and Ajeem fell down on the road and sustained fractures in his right leg.
The petitioner was taken to GTB Hospital, Delhi, where he was treated vide MLC no. A-4201/33/18.

PW1 categorically stated that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle,
otherwise the accident could have been avoided.
13.
The injured/ petitioner (PW1) has been cross-examined on behalf of the respondent no.1 and

on perusal of the cross-examination, this Tribunal finds that nothing has been brought on record during the entire cross-examination of the petitioner, which may challenge his deposition with respect to the rash and negligent driving of the respondent no.1 and thereby causing the accident of the petitioner.

Though on the aspect of rash and negligence of the driver/ respondent no.1, only a few suggestions have been given to the petitioner (PW1) that no such incident of accident has ever occurred in which the offending vehicle was involved or that the alleged accident does not have relation to the respondent no.1 or the other respondent but these suggestions have been promptly denied by the PW1.

Also, it is observed that no supportive material or evidence has been brought on record in support of the said suggestions and therefore, mere giving such suggestions to the petitioner is of no value in the absence of any corroborative evidence.
1 4 .

To find out the veracity of the said defence of R1W1, this Tribunal examined the IO (Investigating Officer)/ ASI Om Prakash under section 168 of Bhartiya Sakshya Adhiniyam.

The IO stated that the Site Plan, which is at page no. 28 of the DAR, was prepared by him at the Dar - Shadab vs Pawan Kumar on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134236865/
4 instance of Ajeem and he (IO) had cross-verified the authenticity of the Site Plan with the site and the Site Plan was found to be a correct representation of the actual site.
IO made it clear that at the time of the accident near the point A, which is the site of accident in the Site Plan, there was no cut on the divider.

In view of the examination of IO, wherein IO clarified that there was no cut on the divider, the story of defence made by the R1W1 that the petitioner was hit by a three-wheeler and not by his truck, does not inspire any confidence.

15. Moreover, as per FIR, which was registered after few hours of the accident, the driver/
respondent no.1 was caught hold by Ajeem, the pillion rider on the motorcycle of petitioner, from the spot of accident itself and the offending truck and the motorcycle of the petitioner with accidental damages were taken into police possession from the spot of accident.

16. Not only this, it is evident from the DAR that respondent no.1 was charge-sheeted in the criminal case by the police after detailed investigation and in a motor vehicle accident claim case, the contents of chargesheet support the version of petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1.

Though the respondent no.1 has been acquitted in the criminal case, the acquittal of the respondent no.1 is not on merit but for the reason that the victim of the accident, i.e., the petitioner could not be served with the summons issued by the criminal court.

17. Besides above, the MLC, prepared at GTB Hospital, Delhi clearly shows that the petitioner/
injured was brought to the hospital in injured condition with the history of RTA (Road Traffic Accident) and further the injuries received by him were opined to be grievous in nature.
18.

Also, it is a settled proposition of law that, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability,
the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
A holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

However, that does not mean that a Tribunal which has been a p p r o a c h e d

a  
c l a i m  
f o r ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 674/2018; Shadab v. Pawan Kumar & Anr. 8 of 20 Pages compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act should ignore all basic principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.
The relevant provisions of the Act are not intended to jettison all principles of law relating to a claim for compensation, which is still based on a tortious liability.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as; New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v.

sentences.text: Thus, in view of the above, this Tribunal finds that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into grievous injuries to the petitioner.
ISSUE NO.2
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
OPP COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 20.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.

As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it s h o u l d b e a p i t t a n c e . " J u s t c o m p e n s a t i o n " c a n n o t b e ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 674/2018; Shadab v. Pawan Kumar & Anr. 9 of 20 Pages equated with bonanza
but it suggests application of fair and equitable principles and reasonable approach of the Tribunal while awarding the compensation.
This reasonableness must be on large peripheral field.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury which he might have received in the accident caused by the motor vehicle in a public place, rather he is compensated for the loss, which he suffered as a result of that injury that he suffered in the accident.

[Ref. Yadava Kumar v. National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
(2010) 10 SCC 34; Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343; Puttamma v. K.L. Narayana Reddy,
(2013) 15 SCC 45]; Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755; Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343.
21.

In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses 22.
The petitioner (PW1) has placed on record medical bills Ex.PW1/1 (colly) for a total sum of Rs.7,495/-.
It is observed that said bills have not been disputed by learned counsel for the respondents during cross-examination of PW1.
Hence, a sum of Rs.7,495/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.
Loss of Income During Treatment 23.

The Discharge Summary of the petitioner, prepared by GTB Hospital, reveals that the petitioner was diagnosed to have suffered "closed fracture of SOF (right)" and the petitioner remained ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 674/2018; Shadab v. Pawan Kumar & Anr. 10 of 20 Pages hospitalized from 08.10.2018 to 19.10.2028.
During hospitalization, his surgical operation was done for treatment of the injuries.

The treatment record Ex.PW1/A (colly) shows that even after being discharged from the hospital, his Dar - Shadab vs Pawan Kumar on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134236865/
6
further treatment continued till December 2018.

Considering the nature of the injury and period of treatment, it may be safely assumed that the petitioner must not have been able to do any work for at least two months after his accident and therefore, the petitioner deserves to be compensated for loss of income of said period during treatment.
24.
Though the petitioner (PW1) has deposed that he was working as a Barber and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, however, he did not produce any documentary evidence in this regard.
The Aadhar Card Ex.PW1/2 of the petitioner shows his residential address of Amroha, U.P.

Since, the petitioner has not been able to bring on record any documentary evidence of his vocation and income, the income of the petitioner has to be taken at par with minimum wages of an unskilled worker of U.P. on the date of accident (07.10.2018), which were Rs.7,676/- per month.

Thus, income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.7,676/- per month and accordingly, a sum of Rs.15,352/-
(7,676x2) is granted to the petitioner on account of loss of income of two months during treatment.

Loss of Future Earnings (due to disability)
25.
As per disability certificate bearing Ex.PW2/1, issued by the Medical Board of GTB Hospital, the petitioner was assessed to have suffered 17% permanent disability in relation to his right lower limb.

The disablement and loss of earning capacity are two different aspects and not substitute for each other and the loss of income has to be seen considering the profession in which the petitioner was engaged at the time of the accident.

In the instant case, PW2 Dr. Sandeep B. Rathod (Senior Resident, Orthopaedic, GTB Hospital, Delhi) proved the disability certificate of the petitioner as Ex.PW2/1, which shows that the petitioner has suffered 17% permanent locomotor disability in relation to right lower limb.
PW2 (doctor) deposed that the petitioner is a case of fracture of the femur shaft (right side) and he will have mild difficulty walking on slopes, squatting and sitting cross-legged.

In view of this, it is safely assumed that the petitioner, who has deposed that he was as Barbar but in absence of any evidence to that effect, has been considered by this Tribunal to be an unskilled worker, would face difficulties to some extent in performing his work.

Hence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that functional disability in relation to the whole body of the petitioner may be considered to be 10% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of his future income.
27. Further, the law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351].

28. As discussed above, the income of the petitioner has been assessed to be Rs.7,676/- per month.

Thus, applying the multiplier of 17 and future prospects @ 40% with 10% loss of income on account of whole-body functional disability, the total loss of future income would come to Rs.2,19,227/-
[10% of (7,676x140/100x17x12)] and the same is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
Special Diet, Conveyance & Attendant Charges 29.
Though the petitioner has not led any specific evidence in respect of the money spent by him towards special diet, transport expenses and attendant charges.
As per discharge summary and treatment record, for the treatment of injuries suffered in the accident, petitioner was diagnosed to have sustained "closed fracture of SOF (right)".

He remained hospitalized for about 12 days from 08.10.2018 to 19.10.2018 and during hospitalization, he had undergone surgery on 17.10.2018 and thereafter, also, his further treatment continued till December 2018.

Considering the nature of injury and the period of treatment, an inference can be drawn that the petitioner had to spend ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 674/2018; Shadab v. Pawan Kumar & Anr. 13 of 20 Pages a reasonable amount on high and rich protein diet for the purpose of early recovery, especially post surgery, as well as for visiting the hospital/ doctor during further treatment.

The petitioner is also required to be granted attendant charges to compensate the work/ job of his family members, which would definitely have suffered in providing assistance to him in his routine activities during treatment period (Refer : DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).

Accordingly, the petitioner is awarded a total sum of Rs.50,000/-
for special diet, conveyance and attendant charges.

NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Pain & Sufferings 30.

While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victims of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No:
709/02, date of decision: 02.02.2007 can be considered:
"12. On account of pain and suffering, suffice, would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of money value.
However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objective co-relation with the pain and suffering.

13. The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:

8 (a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected (c) Duration of the treatment."
31.
In the instant case, as per MLC, the injuries sustained by the petitioner were opined to be grievous in nature.
The petitioner sustained "closed fracture of SOF (right)".

Thus, it is clear that d u e ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 674/2018; Shadab v. Pawan Kumar & Anr. 14 of 20 Pages to the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner during his treatment must have gone through immense pain and suffering,
for which Rs.25,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
Loss of Amenities 32.

It is evident that even after completion of treatment, the petitioner suffered 20% permanent disability, which has been assessed by this Tribunal to be 10% functional disability in relation to the whole body of the petitioner.

It may be safely assumed that with the aforementioned disability,
petitioner will not be able to enjoy the amenities of life to the fullest.
Hence, an amount of Rs.50,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.

33. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-

 2. Loss of Earnings (During Treatment) Rs.15,352/-
4. Loss of Future Earnings (Due to Disability) Rs.2,19,227/-
Special Diet, Conveyance & Attendant Rs.50,000/-
5. Charges 6. Pain & Sufferings Rs.25,000/-

Thus, the compensation in this case comes to Rs.3,67,074/-.
INTEREST Dar - Shadab vs Pawan Kumar on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134236865/
9 34. The petitioner shall also be entitled for interest @ 7% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of petition till realization.

Now, admittedly, the offending vehicle was not insured at the time of accident and therefore, the respondent no.1 Pawan Kumar being the driver of the offending vehicle is the principal tortfeasor whereas the respondent no.2 EDMC being registered owner of the offending vehicle, would have vicarious liability.
Therefore, it is held that respondent no.1 and 2 shall pay the entire compensation/ award amount to the petitioner, jointly and/ or severally.
RELIEF 36.

In the light of the decision on substantive issues framed, the present claim petition is allowed and the following award is being passed:
AWARD 37.
The mode of disbursement shall be decided after compliance of the award.

The interim compensation, if any, shall be adjusted against this award amount along with the waiver of interest, if any, as directed by the Tribunal during the pendency of this case.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Though the respondent no.1 has been acquitted in the criminal case, the acquittal of the respondent no.1 is not on merit but for the reason that the victim of the accident, i.e., the petitioner could not be served with the summons issued by the criminal court.
Also, it is a settled proposition of law that, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability,
the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
A holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
The relevant provisions of the Act are not intended to jettison all principles of law relating to a claim for compensation, which is still based on a tortious liability.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as; New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v.
Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Dar - Shadab vs Pawan Kumar on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134236865/
5 Variyal & Ors., (2007) 5 SCC 428.
19.
but it suggests application of fair and equitable principles and reasonable approach of the Tribunal while awarding the compensation.
This reasonableness must be on large peripheral field.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury which he might have received in the accident caused by the motor vehicle in a public place, rather he is compensated for the loss, which he suffered as a result of that injury that he suffered in the accident.
[Ref. Yadava Kumar v. National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
(2010) 10 SCC 34; Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343; Puttamma v. K.L. Narayana Reddy,
(2013) 15 SCC 45]; Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755; Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343.
21.
Loss of Future Earnings (due to disability)
25.
As per disability certificate bearing Ex.PW2/1, issued by the Medical Board of GTB Hospital, the petitioner was assessed to have suffered 17% permanent disability in relation to his right lower limb.
The disablement and loss of earning capacity are two different aspects and not substitute for each other and the loss of income has to be seen considering the profession in which the petitioner was engaged at the time of the accident.
Hence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that functional disability in relation to the whole body of the petitioner may be considered to be 10% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of his future income.
27. Further, the law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351].
The Aadhaar Card of the petitioner (Ex.PW1/2) reflects his date of birth as 01.01.1991, which would mean that he was 27 years of age on the date of accident (07.10.2018) and thus, a multiplier of 17 as applicable to age group between 26-30 years, would be applicable as per settled principle laid down in case of S a r l a V e r m a v . D T C ( 2 0 0 9 ) 6 S C C 1 2 1 .

Pawan Kumar & Anr. 13 of 20 Pages a reasonable amount on high and rich protein diet for the purpose of early recovery, especially post surgery, as well as for visiting the hospital/ doctor during further treatment.
In the instant case, as per MLC, the injuries sustained by the petitioner were opined to be grievous in nature.
The petitioner sustained "closed fracture of SOF (right)".
It is evident that even after completion of treatment, the petitioner suffered 20% permanent disability, which has been assessed by this Tribunal to be 10% functional disability in relation to the whole body of the petitioner.
It may be safely assumed that with the aforementioned disability,
petitioner will not be able to enjoy the amenities of life to the fullest.
